title: Introduce lint rule registry and adaptive merge prober
author: Asha Banerjee
description: Context: Our presubmit lint surface has grown organically: multiple rule sources (team-level config, language plugins, and repo-wide overrides) make it hard to apply targeted fixes, and merge noise for low-value rules is spiking. This PR extracts a centralized 'lint rule registry' and pairs it with an 'adaptive merge prober' that samples merges to validate rule changes before broad rollout. Motivation: reduce noisy failures, enable safe rule rollouts, and provide a single place for rule provenance and automated rollback heuristics. What this PR does (high level): 1) Introduces a lint rule registry service (in tools/lintrun/registry) that normalizes rules from .lintrc, team manifests, and language plugins into a single canonical format with provenance metadata (source, team, rationales, rule-risk). 2) Adds a small translation layer so existing runners (python/ts/go linters) can consume registry snapshots without changing language plugin code. 3) Adds an adaptive merge prober in CI: new rule rollouts are initially enabled for a configurable fraction of merges; the prober collects failure/flake signals and can auto-quiet or rollback rules when noise exceeds thresholds. 4) Adds observability: rule-level metrics (rule.fail_rate, rule.flake_rate), rollout telemetry, and an alert guard for noisy rollouts. 5) Includes a migration tool (scripts/lintrun/migrate_rules.py) to generate registry snapshots from current repo configs and a small CLI to preview rollout effects locally. Design notes: - Registry stores rules as typed YAML with fields: id, pattern, severity, owner_team, introduced_by_pr, risk_score, exemptions. - Rollouts are staged via annotations on PRs and a per-branch rollout configuration. The adaptive prober implements stage-aware sampling (canary -> progressive -> full) and uses weighted-failure windows to decide automatic backoff. - To avoid surprising teams, initial rollout policy is conservative: 5% canary for 24h, then 25% progressive for 72h, then full. Migration plan: - Step 1 (this PR): add registry and translation, run CI with registry read-only and preview telemetry. - Step 2: opt-in teams can publish manifest refs to registry and try staged rollouts. - Step 3: full migration after 2 weeks of canary telemetry and one successful rollback cycle test. Testing and safety: - Unit tests for registry normalization and translation layer. - End-to-end smoke job in a gated CI lane that runs rule snapshots against a small corpus to estimate flakiness. - Manual rollback path: an emergency-silence label that disables new rules immediately. Rollout checklist (tickboxes maintained in PR body): [x] Registry normalization logic and unit tests added. [x] Translation adapters for python/ts/go runners. [x] Migration script and sample snapshot. [x] Observability dashboards and alerting rules defined. [x] Documentation: how to add rules and how staged rollouts work. Related work: builds on prior presubmit-sampling work (ENG-2150) and ties into the dep-stability telemetry pipeline. Known limitations: - Registry is initially single-region and stored in repo; future work will add a lightweight service backed by object storage and signing. - Some legacy language plugins with embedded rules still need small adapters. Impact: expected to reduce noisy presubmit failures by surfacing provenance and letting noisy rules be isolated or rolled back without full repo churn.

review_comments: Marco Li (review): The registry schema looks good but can we reduce the required fields to make adoption easier for teams? Example: make 'rationales' optional.
Author reply (Asha): Agreed. Made 'rationales' optional and added a migration note in docs/lintrun/rollouts.md.
Jordan Kim (review): The prober decision window uses a 10m sliding window — seems tight for flaky network tests. Suggest 1h for the initial rollout.
Author reply (Asha): Updated prober defaults to 1h window with adaptive backoff multiplier; added override per-branch in prober.yaml.
Priya Das (approval): Verified translation adapters against go/python/ts linters on a small sample corpus. Observability hooks emit rule.fail_rate as expected. Approving.

merge_summary: Squash merged by Marco Li after approvals. Forward-ported a small config change to release/v2026-02 in a follow-up commit. Release gating: no user-facing API change. Registry is behind opt-in flags by default.
release_notes: Add: lint rule registry and adaptive merge prober to enable staged rule rollouts and reduce noisy presubmit failures. Opt-in via docs/lintrun/rollouts.md. No breaking changes.
